concept.title: Clustering: finding the towns on the map
concept.shortdesc: Clustering looks for the places where listings crowd together; each crowded area is a candidate category.

conbody.p: Once every listing has a position, a clustering method looks for the places where listings crowd together. It is much like picking out towns on a night-time satellite photograph by their lights.
Each crowded area is a candidate category.

Listings out on their own are set aside as fitting nowhere. They are not forced into the nearest group. They are useful: they show where the picture has gaps and which records need a person to look at them.
The project uses two standard methods together, known as UMAP and HDBSCAN. The first simplifies the map so the crowds are easier to see. The second finds them.
